proposed.explanation:
Your friend's numbers are wrong on both counts. The audited FY2025 consolidated statement (unit L.E. (000)) shows net profit of 22,578,063 × 1,000 = 22,578,063,000 EGP (≈ 22.6 bn), not 225.9 bn. The FY2024 figure is 10,111,328 × 1,000 = 10,111,328,000 EGP (≈ 10.1 bn). The year-on-year multiple is about 2.2×, not 'more than ten times.' Your friend appears to have misread the thousands-unit figure as if it were already in millions.

That said, the underlying growth is genuinely strong: revenue rose ~31 % (81.7 bn → 106.7 bn) and net profit more than doubled, with the net margin expanding from roughly 12 % to 21 %. Leverage improved (total liabilities fell from ~3.3× equity to ~2.6×), though a D/E of ~2.55× is still high for a telecom.

Why not put all 50,000 EGP into ETEL:
• You already hold 150 shares worth 21,292.50 EGP, about 30 % of the 71,292.50 EGP portfolio. Buying all 50,000 EGP in ETEL would push the single-stock weight to roughly 70 %, far beyond the 50 % diversification cap and well outside what a medium-risk, 5-year-horizon profile comfortably supports.
• The evidence covers only two fiscal years. The dramatic margin expansion (12 % → 21 %) could include one-off items, FX effects, or a weak-2024 base. There is no 3- or 5-year trend, no operating-cash-flow, capex, dividend, or segment data to confirm the growth is structural.
• ETEL is a single-country, single-sector, highly leveraged name. A sector-specific or macro shock could produce a 30-50 % drawdown, which sits at the upper edge of your stated loss tolerance.

Why a modest 50-share buy is still reasonable:
• The verified growth is substantial and the balance-sheet trajectory is improving.
• At 141.95 EGP per share, 50 shares cost 7,097.50 EGP, leaving 42,902.50 EGP in cash. The ETEL position rises to 200 shares (28,390 EGP), or about 40 % of the portfolio – a meaningful but not excessive increase, and comfortably under the 50 % cap.
• Keeping ~43,000 EGP in cash preserves the ability to diversify into other names or wait for a better entry, which is prudent given the limited evidence and your medium risk profile.

Risks and uncertainty: This is guidance, not a guarantee. The two-year data window is the main limitation; if the margin expansion proves to be a one-off, the earnings base could normalise. The high leverage means interest-rate or revenue shocks would hit equity hard. Egyptian-listed equities carry country, currency, and regulatory risk. The 5-year horizon is workable but not long enough to fully absorb a deep single-stock drawdown and recover. Monitor the next annual report for confirmation that the margin and growth are sustainable before considering any further additions.

reports.financial:
# Telecom Egypt (ETEL) – Evidence Analysis

## 1. Correcting the Friend's Claim

The friend's statement is **wrong on both counts**.

| Figure | Friend's claim | Actual (from evidence) |
|---|---|---|
| 2025 net profit | 225.9 billion EGP | **22,578,063,000 EGP ≈ 22.58 bn EGP** [ETEL-ETEL_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_en-p6-35] (22,578,063 × 1,000, unit L.E.(000)) |
| 2024 net profit | (implied ≈ 22.6 bn) | **10,111,328,000 EGP ≈ 10.11 bn EGP** [ETEL-ETEL_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_en-p6-36] |
| Multiple | "more than ten times" | **≈ 2.23×** (22,578,063 ÷ 10,111,328) |

The friend appears to have misread the thousands-unit figure (22,578,063) as if it were already in millions, inflating the number ten-fold. The profit did roughly **double**, not multiply ten-fold.

---

## 2. Profitability & Growth (FY2025 vs FY2024)

All figures converted from L.E.(000) to whole EGP.

| Metric | FY2025 | FY2024 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operating revenue | 106,672,946,000 EGP [ETEL-ETEL_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_en-p6-01] | 81,677,812,000 EGP [ETEL-ETEL_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_en-p6-02] | +30.6 % |
| Net profit | 22,578,063,000 EGP [ETEL-ETEL_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_en-p6-35] | 10,111,328,000 EGP [ETEL-ETEL_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_en-p6-36] | +123.3 % |
| Net margin (NP ÷ Revenue) | ≈ 21.2 % | ≈ 12.4 % | +8.8 pp |
| EPS (L.E. / share) | 11.93 [ETEL-ETEL_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_en-p6-55] | 4.79 [ETEL-ETEL_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_en-p6-56] | +149.1 % |

> **Unit note on EPS:** The page-level unit line reads "L.E.(000)", but the row heading explicitly states "L.E. / Share" and the values (11.93, 4.79) are clearly per-share EGP, not thousands. I treat them as **11.93 EGP** and **4.79 EGP** per share. Flagged as a minor **AMBIGUOUS** unit label in the printed report; no computation is affected because the per-share values are unambiguous in context.

The profit jump is substantial and is driven by both top-line growth (~31 %) and a large margin expansion (~12 % → ~21 %).

---

## 3. Balance-Sheet Snapshot (Consolidated)

| Item | 31/12/2025 | 31/12/2024 (reclassified) |
|---|---|---|
| Total assets | 225,882,527,000 EGP [ETEL-ETEL_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_en-p5-31] | 197,952,788,000 EGP [ETEL-ETEL_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_en-p5-31] |
| Total equity | 63,687,826,000 EGP [ETEL-ETEL_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_en-p5-45] | 45,937,991,000 EGP [ETEL-ETEL_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_en-p5-45] |
| Implied total liabilities (Assets − Equity) | ≈ 162,194,701,000 EGP | ≈ 152,014,797,000 EGP |
| Debt-to-equity (liabilities ÷ equity) | ≈ **2.55×** | ≈ **3.31×** |

- Equity grew ~38.6 % y/y, outpacing the ~14.1 % asset growth, so leverage **improved** (D/E fell from ~3.3× to ~2.5×).
- Even so, a D/E of 2.55× is still a **highly leveraged** capital structure for a telecom operator. The company carries roughly 162 bn EGP of liabilities against 64 bn EGP of equity.

---

## 4. Risks & Data-Quality Flags

| # | Item | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | **Leverage** | D/E ≈ 2.55× [computed from p5-31, p5-45]. A downturn in revenue or a rise in interest rates would pressure the already-thin equity cushion. |
| R2 | **Concentration / single-stock risk** | The investor's entire equity sleeve is ETEL (150 sh × 141.95 = 21,292.50 EGP). Adding the full 50,000 EGP cash would make ETEL ≈ 70 % of the 71,292.50 EGP portfolio. |
| R3 | **Valuation context** | At 141.95 EGP/share the market is pricing EPS of 11.93 EGP at a P/E of ≈ 11.9×. Whether that is cheap or fair depends on the sustainability of the 21 % margin, which is not yet multi-year evidence. |
| R4 | **One-year data only** | The evidence set covers FY2025 and FY2024. There is no 3- or 5-year trend to confirm the margin expansion is structural rather than a one-off (e.g., one-time items, FX revaluation, or a base-effect from a weak 2024). |
| R5 | **AMBIGUOUS unit on EPS row** | Page unit "L.E.(000)" conflicts with the row label "L.E. / Share". Values used as per-share EGP; no computation affected, but flagged for transparency. |
| R6 | **No dividend, cash-flow, or segment data** | The evidence provided does not include operating cash flow, capex, dividend policy, or segment breakdown, limiting the depth of the analysis. |

---

## 5. Relevance to the Investor's Profile

- **Goal / horizon:** Top-up retirement savings over 5 years. A single, highly leveraged Egyptian-listed telecom is a concentrated, single-country, single-sector bet.
- **Risk tolerance:** Medium willingness and medium ability to withstand losses. A 2.55× D/E company in a single emerging market can see share prices swing 30-50 % in a stress scenario; that is at the upper edge of "medium" tolerance.
- **Liquidity:** The investor keeps a separate emergency fund, so the 50,000 EGP cash is not a liquidity buffer. However, deploying 100 % of it into one stock eliminates the ability to diversify or wait for a better entry.
- **Current exposure:** ETEL is already ~30 % of the portfolio. Adding all 50,000 EGP would push it to ~70 %, a significant concentration step.

---

## 6. Summary of Findings (no action recommendation)

- The friend's "225.9 bn / 10×" story is **incorrect**; the verified figures are **22.58 bn EGP** in 2025 vs **10.11 bn EGP** in 2024, a **2.2×** increase [ETEL-ETEL_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_en-p6-35, p6-36].
- The underlying business showed **strong FY2025 growth** (revenue +31 %, net profit +123 %, EPS +149 %) and **improving leverage** (D/E 3.3× → 2.5×).
- However, the evidence set is **limited to two fiscal years**, the balance sheet remains **highly leveraged**, and the investor's profile (medium risk, 5-year horizon, single-country exposure) raises **concentration and volatility concerns** if the entire cash balance is added to one position.
- I have **not** been asked to, and do not, recommend a buy, sell, or hold. The decision agent should weigh the above evidence against the investor's full portfolio, diversification policy, and risk limits.
reports.investor:
## Fact-check on your friend's numbers

Your friend has misread the figures. The audited consolidated statement (p. 6, unit L.E. (000)) shows:

| | 31/12/2025 | 31/12/2024 |
|---|---|---|
| Net profit for the year | 22,578,063 × 1,000 = **≈ 22.6 billion EGP** | 10,111,328 × 1,000 = **≈ 10.1 billion EGP** |

- The 2025 profit is roughly **22.6 billion**, not 225.9 billion. Your friend appears to have shifted a decimal (or dropped the "thousands" multiplier).
- The 2025 figure is about **2.2×** the 2024 figure, not "more than ten times."

So the headline is directionally right (profit grew substantially) but the magnitude is off by an order of magnitude.

---

## Suitability assessment

### Horizon & goal
A 5-year horizon aimed at topping up retirement savings is workable for equity exposure, but it is not a long enough runway to absorb a deep single-stock drawdown and recover fully. Medium loss-willingness and medium financial capacity to absorb losses reinforce that a large, undiversified equity position is at the upper edge of what is comfortable.

### Liquidity
You keep a separate emergency fund, so the 50,000 EGP cash in this portfolio is not earmarked for short-term bills. That is a point in favour of committing some of it to a longer-holding asset. However, "free" does not mean "all at once into one ticker."

### Current concentration
| Item | Value (EGP) |
|---|---|
| Cash | 50,000.00 |
| ETEL – 150 sh × 141.95 | 21,292.50 |
| **Total portfolio** | **71,292.50** |

ETEL already represents **≈ 30 %** of the portfolio. If the entire 50,000 EGP cash were added to ETEL, the single-stock weight would jump to **≈ 59 %** of a 121,292.50 EGP portfolio. For an investor with medium loss tolerance and a 5-year window, that level of single-name concentration is a significant risk factor: a sector-specific or company-specific shock would dominate the whole portfolio.

### What the portfolio allows
- **Sellable:** 150 ETEL shares (≈ 21,293 EGP at the cutoff price) – you could reduce or exit the position if you wished to rebalance.
- **Free cash:** 50,000 EGP – not tied to any near-term obligation given the separate emergency fund.
- **No other holdings** are listed, so there is no existing diversification to lean on.

### How much cash could reasonably be committed
Given medium loss willingness/capacity, a 5-year horizon, and the existing 30 % ETEL weight, committing **all** 50,000 EGP to the same single stock would push concentration well beyond what the stated risk profile comfortably supports. A more measured approach would keep the single-stock share of the total portfolio within a range that a medium-risk investor can tolerate (the team would set that threshold), and would consider whether the remaining cash is better allocated to a broader basket or held in a lower-volatility instrument while the retirement goal is still 5 years out.

---

### Bottom line for your question

1. **The friend's numbers are wrong** – profit was ≈ 22.6 bn, not 225.9 bn, and the year-on-year multiple is ≈ 2.2×, not >10×.
2. **Putting all 50,000 EGP into more ETEL** would take a single stock from ~30 % to ~59 % of your portfolio. With a 5-year horizon, medium loss tolerance, and no other holdings to offset, that is a concentration step that sits at the aggressive end of what your stated profile supports. The portfolio *allows* you to do it (the cash is free, the shares are liquid), but the suitability profile does not clearly *support* doing it in full.

I'm flagging the fit, not recommending a trade. The next step for the team would be to decide the target single-stock cap and the allocation split for the 50,000 EGP.
